method: Form-specific publisher/author references; original teaching examples must be written separately. No source examples imported. Earlier mappings are bridges/contrasts, not new official N3 requirements.

notes.formation: Verb ます-stem + そう; い-adjective without final い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう. Follow with だ/です, な before a noun, に as an adverb. いい gives よさそう. Negative attachment has further distinctions; do not score it before explicit instruction.
notes.teachingChoice: Retrieve N4 appearance rather than rebrand it as new N3 grammar. Give perceptual cues and distinguish stem 降りそう from a reported plain proposition 降るそう. Do not use a numerical confidence scale.

notes.form: reported そうだ / inferential-hearsay らしい
notes.formation: Reported そうだ follows a plain proposition, including noun/な-adjective + だ. Inferential らしい attaches directly to nonpast nouns/な-adjective stems and to plain verbs/い-adjectives. Distinguish the characteristic noun + らしい use from hearsay; do not equate all らしい with a quotation.
notes.teachingChoice: These readings can overlap. A hearsay question must identify what was reported and by whom, or explicitly request a taught construction; no ambiguous そうだ versus らしい answer contest. Don't claim hearsay proves the proposition true.

notes.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective clause + ようだ; noun + のようだ; な-adjective + なようだ. ような modifies a noun and ように modifies an action. Inference differs from purpose ように and changed ability ようになる taught in unit 1.
notes.teachingChoice: Use clues in a notice or observed room, and give the inference a basis. Do not turn apparent evidence into absolute truth or a graded certainty ranking.

notes.formation: Plain clauses or noun/な-adjective stems + みたいだ; みたいな + noun; みたいに + action. This みたい is not verb-stem 見たい meaning want to see.
notes.teachingChoice: A conversational resemblance/inference contrast with ようだ. These can both fit many contexts; score connector/form tasks or an explicit situation, not an unstated preference.

notes.formation: Conventional noun/stem + っぽい forms become い-adjectives: っぽく, っぽかった, っぽくない. Not freely combinable with every verb/adjective. Teach selected established forms, not arbitrary invented derivations.
notes.teachingChoice: Perceived trait is not an identity claim or medical/personality diagnosis. Distinguish a stereotypical expectation in characteristic らしい from resemblance/tendency, without gender generalisations. Meaning and register are context-dependent.
